Diagnose a spec against its data

Source: R/spec-fields.R
spec_diagnose.Rd

spec_diagnose() checks a spec (a list, JSON string, or path) or a built PlotSpec without throwing: it parses it, validates every referenced field against the data, runs a few pre-compile checks, dry-run compiles it, and reports per layer how many rows will not be shown. It returns a structured verdict. vplot_from_spec() is the strict form — it returns the PlotSpec on success and raises a classed vellumplot_spec_invalid error (carrying the same diagnostics) on failure.

Usage

spec_diagnose(spec, data = NULL, env = globalenv())

vplot_from_spec(spec, data = NULL, env = globalenv())

Arguments

spec

A spec list (from as_spec()), a JSON string, a .json path, or a PlotSpec.

data

The data frame the spec is drawn from. Required when the spec stores data by reference; optional (for field validation) when inlined. Ignored for a PlotSpec, which carries its own data.

env

Environment channel expressions are re-quoted in.

Value

spec_diagnose() returns a list of class vellumplot_diagnosis with ok (logical), plot (the PlotSpec or NULL), diagnostics (a list of records with severity, field, message, hint), and report (a data frame with one row per layer: layer, mark, rows, the counts missing, transform, stat, limits, their total dropped, and oob, the rows outside a scale's limits that are still drawn; NULL when the plot could not be built). Printing it shows a summary. vplot_from_spec() returns a PlotSpec.

Details

This is the agent repair loop: a failure comes back as data an agent can act on (which field is unknown, the nearest real field) rather than a traceback.

Pre-compile checks

Before compiling, the plot is checked for mistakes that would compile to a wrong plot or fail with an opaque error:

  • a facet variable missing from the plot data (an error), or from a layer's own data (a warning: that layer is then repeated across that variable's panels);

  • color (or fill) mapped to variables of different type in two layers (one continuous, one discrete), although the layers share one scale and legend (an error, or a warning when the scale kind is set explicitly);

  • a manual or discrete palette (scale_color_manual(), ...) on a continuous colour channel, which the compile refuses (an error).

Compile report

Some rows produce no visible mark. The report element counts them per layer, on the layer's input rows, attributing each row to the first reason that applies:

  • missing: a continuous position value (x, y, xend, ymin, ...) is NA. Such a row is removed from the plot with a warning, or leaves a gap in a line, step or area;

  • transform: the axis transform cannot map the value, e.g. a value <= 0 on a log axis;

  • stat: the layer's statistic leaves the row out, e.g. an infinite value in a histogram or density, or a group with too few points for a density, a smooth or an ellipse;

  • limits: the value is outside explicit scale limits (lims(), scale_*(limits = )), so it is clipped away. Coordinate limits (coord_cartesian(xlim = )) zoom instead and are not counted.

Their total is dropped. Limits follow each scale's oob handler: a position outside its limits counts under limits when it is clipped (the default) or censored, and so does a censored size. A separate column, oob, counts rows that are outside a scale's limits but still drawn: a squished position, or a colour, fill, size, alpha or linewidth value (clamped to the end of the palette, given the NA colour, or extrapolated). They are not part of dropped.

A missing non-position value (colour, size, ...) is drawn with the scale's NA value, a missing discrete position as a trailing "NA" category, and a missing facet value in a trailing "NA" panel, so none of them is counted. Each layer that loses rows also adds a "warning" diagnostic, so it shows in the printed summary.

See also

spec_fields(), spec_schema(), vplot_ask()

Examples

spec <- as_spec(vplot(mtcars) |> mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg))
d <- spec_diagnose(spec, data = mtcars)
d$ok
#> [1] TRUE

# a PlotSpec works too; the report shows rows a log axis cannot draw
df <- data.frame(x = 1:4, y = c(-1, 1, 10, NA))
p <- vplot(df) |>
  mark_point(x = x, y = y) |>
  scale_y_continuous(trans = "log10")
spec_diagnose(p)
#> Warning: NaNs produced
#> Warning: NaNs produced
#> <vellumplot diagnosis> ok: 0 errors, 1 warning
#> * [warning] Layer 1 (point): 2 of 4 rows will not be shown: 1 missing a position value, 1 not mappable on a transformed axis (e.g. <= 0 on a log scale).
#>     See `$report` for the per-layer counts.
#> 
#> Rows not shown, per layer (`oob`: drawn, outside a scale's limits):
#>  layer  mark rows missing transform stat limits dropped oob
#>      1 point    4       1         1    0      0       2   0
